subject.title: [Bug] Agent context window fragmentation during concurrent subagent tool calls

question: Should concurrent native Codex subagent results remain available in completion order with identifier-based correlation, or must OpenClaw impose invocation-order delivery even when that blocks faster children?
rationale: Both policies are technically possible but have different latency and upstream-compatibility semantics; source inspection does not establish the reporter’s proposed invocation-order policy as the existing contract.

options.title: Keep completion order
options.body: Require a correlation trace, retain responsive completion-order delivery, and fix only a proven identifier-association defect at the Codex harness boundary.

options.title: Enforce invocation order
options.body: Specify invocation-order delivery as a product contract and accept head-of-line blocking plus dedicated buffering and lifecycle tests.

options.title: Close after diagnostic
options.body: If the focused trace shows correct result association and no user-visible confusion, close the report as not reproducible.

recommendation.title: Keep completion order
recommendation.body: Require a correlation trace, retain responsive completion-order delivery, and fix only a proven identifier-association defect at the Codex harness boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged context-lifecycle work defines the current Codex/OpenClaw ownership and projection boundary most directly implicated by an ordering-policy choice.
